issues.issue: Guest authentication and UserType are independent; distinguish invited external guests and Teams standard channels from shared channels.
Invented Conditional Access bulk-upload and subscription CSV distractors are implausible; bulk creation is an asynchronous job, not atomic provisioning.
Mail-enabled security groups exist in Exchange Online; a Microsoft 365 group does not automatically create a Team, and its group mailbox is not a standalone shared mailbox.
Rule example uses noncanonical single-quoted values and does not state Member status or attribute population; evaluation is asynchronous.
Group name does not define its rule; department versus city is inconsistent, and another assignment could preserve the same license.
Access controls also include session controls; original definition omits them.
IMAP/POP are not inherently legacy authentication: OAuth clients exist; target resources and enabled policy state were unstated.
An exclusion from one policy does not guarantee no MFA prompt; other policies and existing MFA claims matter.
An app password is an obvious nonfactor distractor; avoid the undefined superlative strongest.
Enforced per-user MFA does not prompt on every sign-in; remembered sessions and valid MFA claims exist.
Eligible assignment does not erase permissions from other roles; active does not mean permanent.
Maximum activation duration does not establish the duration actually requested.
Reviewing guests does not automatically remove every route to a resource group; nonresponses need an explicit fallback decision.
Legacy ID Protection policies retire October 1, 2026; original explanation incorrectly says policies can never be tenant-wide.
Password remediation requires MFA/SSPR readiness and supported account configuration; overlaps with 014, so make this test prerequisites rather than repeat risk mapping.
Contributor does not exclude all Microsoft.Authorization operations.
Union of grants is accurate, but cannot imply bypassing denies, policies or locks.
Deny assignments may exclude principals; Owner can sometimes change the protecting stack, though the current delete is denied.
Unrestricted User Access Administrator can grant itself Owner; original requirement incorrectly implies a security boundary against escalation.
Append can deny conflicting requests; DeployIfNotExists is not automatic remediation of all existing resources.
ReadOnly locks affect the control plane, not all writes inside the VM; options B and C were duplicates.
Any scope wrongly includes management groups; prefer Modify for tag inheritance.
Tenant root management group is also defensible unless unrelated subscriptions are explicitly excluded.
UserType does not determine where credentials are managed.
Microsoft 365 group mailbox/Team and role-assignable group distinctions.
Use supported expression syntax and asynchronous evaluation.
Session controls omitted.
Protocols can use OAuth; legacy authentication is not equivalent to IMAP/POP/SMTP.
Active assignments need not be permanent.
Use risk-based Conditional Access terminology.
Remediation prerequisites omitted.
Locks do not protect the data plane.
Management-group locks do not exist.
Named locations need not be trusted or IP-only; risk response uses Conditional Access.
Append and DeployIfNotExists explanation overpromises remediation.
Azure AD B2C is a distinct legacy offering, not simply renamed into External ID.
Premium Files supports NFS too; avoid unmanaged-disk recommendations and an unsupported universally lowest-cost claim.
Very low latency is vague; anchor the selection to the specified premium block-blob workload and HNS capability.
Geo-replication is asynchronous and cannot guarantee zero loss; access tier is a weak redundancy distractor.
Applications must use the secondary endpoint; failover is not solely Microsoft initiated.
Impossible starting configuration: premium page blob accounts support LRS, not ZRS; premium redundancy options are not identical.
RA-GZRS uses LRS in the secondary, not ZRS in both regions; GRS and GZRS have the same published durability target.
Cold is online with fast access, not hours-scale retrieval; original few-hours deadline made Archive ambiguous.
Set Blob Tier also rehydrates archive data; copying is not mandatory.
Lifecycle age is selected explicitly by condition; creation time can be used and there is no universal default.
Tag-based filtering is defensible if configured; use actual prefix mistakes instead of an unnecessary alternate workflow.
Versioning must be enabled before the overwrite and supported for the account.
Stored access-policy changes can take up to 30 seconds; instant revocation promise is false.
Disabling an Entra user is not a reliable immediate invalidation mechanism for an issued bearer SAS.
Zero downtime requires client verification; deletion/wait distractor is nonsensical.
Private endpoints are per storage service and do not automatically disable the public endpoint.
Service endpoints require public network access enabled for selected networks; not a private endpoint.
User delegation SAS is constrained by issuer RBAC/ACL permissions; logging must be configured rather than assumed.
AzCopy sync can also upload recursively and does not delete by default; original A and B both defensible.
Device-code login may use another machine; account keys are not a generic AzCopy blob-auth method.
Portal Cloud Shell is an artificially weak distractor; specify standalone desktop app.
Sync is asynchronous, not instantaneous global consistency.
Premium page blob LRS-only and Files protocol support corrected.
GZRS secondary is LRS; geo copies may lag.
Customer-managed failover exists and clients must use the secondary URL.
Cold latency and archive rehydration corrected.
Lifecycle clocks are explicit.
SAS does not simply follow user disablement.
Disabling public access blocks service-endpoint access too.
Account setting permits/prohibits anonymous access, but access level is container-specific.
Instant SAS revocation is false.
Secondary region is not zone-redundant.
Availability sets can require deallocating every member; scope question to standalone VM.
Temporary disk loss is possible, not an exhaustive guaranteed event list; Linux device names vary.
Ultra limit is outdated; Premium SSD v2 also offers independently adjustable performance and submillisecond latency.
Custom Script does not rerun on unchanged deployments; reboot/domain-join scripts require care, and non-extension distractors are weak.
Never simultaneous is too broad outside planned maintenance.
Zone-spread VMs do not automatically make the application healthy or implement failover.
Uniform instances can be addressed/managed individually too; use the standard VM resource/API distinction.
Default removes highest instance ID after balancing, not strictly newest creation time.
Rollback concerns the failing instance OS disk and configured behavior; manual OS trigger differs from all manual rolling updates.
Explanation confuses availability-set 99.95%, multi-zone 99.99%, and disk-dependent single-VM SLAs.
Never means no automatic restart after exit, not exactly-once execution semantics.
Multiple containers in a group require Linux; volumes must actually be configured for sharing.
Free SKU distractor is fabricated and content-trust aside is unnecessary; replace with plausible configuration error.
Requests are not exact usage caps; App Service also runs containers, so explanation was wrong.
Basic allows manual scale-out, not Azure Monitor autoscale.
Instant rollback and unconditional zero downtime overpromise database/session behavior.
Basic now supports automatic and custom backups; Standard minimum answer is outdated.
Basic/Standard/Premium already use dedicated workers; ASE additionally isolates the environment/frontend.
Premium SSD v2 also satisfies original low-latency independent tuning description.
Temporary storage durability overstated and resize not invariably destructive.
Swap is not instant rollback of database effects.
Notice is at least 30 seconds when Azure schedules eviction; restart depends on capacity.
Zone-spread application architecture does not itself supply platform failover for every resource.
VMSS need not be identical; slot swaps are not an unconditional zero-downtime promise.
VMSS fleets need not be identical and load balancing is not automatic.
Gateway /27 statement needs a non-Basic SKU; old Basic /29 support makes the generic minimum ambiguous.
ARM dynamic private IPs persist through deallocation; original reason for choosing Static is false.
A private endpoint does not disable public network access automatically; Azure service-endpoint traffic is not ordinary public-internet traffic.
App Service subnet sharing with supported plans is possible; distinguish other resource types from additional app plans.
Direct peering is one solution, not the only possible design; specify no transit infrastructure.
VpnGw4 Gen2 is 5 Gbps and non-AZ; original marked answer satisfies neither stated requirement.
Wrong subnet arithmetic: 10.0.1.5 is not in 10.0.0.0/24; the original has no correctly reasoned answer.
Default outbound rules allow VirtualNetwork and Internet, then deny the rest; NSG permission does not create routing/SNAT.
Union is the wrong permissions model; independent NSG evaluation must both allow.
One subnet per VM distractor is implausible.
Basic Load Balancer is retired; HA ports is an internal Standard LB feature, not a public LB outbound-rule combination.
Private frontend alone does not restrict which private networks can reach it; health-probe absolute is unnecessarily broad.
Per-VM public IP is also a defensible SNAT fix without a no-public-IP constraint; 64,000 should be 64,512 and no guarantee of eliminating exhaustion.
Front Door is also defensible unless the wrong claim is part of the answer; make the regional service requirement explicit.
Custom resolvers/forwarders can resolve without a local zone link; state Azure-provided DNS and no forwarding.
Gateway subnet minimum varies with Basic versus non-Basic.
Private endpoint alone does not disable public access.
All outbound is overbroad.
Clarify independent evaluation and new flows.
Do not teach retired Basic as a new deployment choice; HA ports internal-only.
Avoid universal probe claim; separate balancing from targeted NAT.
Correct port count and private DNS forwarding exception.
Front Door failover is not instantaneous.
Active-active does not keep a failed instance tunnel up; Microsoft peering also reaches Azure public services.
Logs can also contain numerical CPU data; specify native platform metric rather than dismissing logs as unsuitable.
Classic Application Insights is retired; workspace-based Application Insights also uses Log Analytics.
Only/most-complete distractors cue the answer; not all metrics export and partner destinations also exist.
take/arg_max do not generally return first chronological event.
Original query averages all VMs and processor instances; identify the target and total CPU counter.
Long-term retention is the current name, needs total-retention duration, and old data is retrieved through search jobs rather than ordinary interactive queries.
project can also compute columns; make preservation of all existing columns the distinguishing requirement.
UserId and EmployeeId do not necessarily share semantics; union supports different schemas.
A log alert is valid too; specify the native signal without guest ingestion.
Mute actions is not a universal alert type setting; changing frequency could also reduce notifications unless evaluation must remain fixed.
Choose direct action types, not interchangeable integration chains.
New NSG flow logs cannot be created; packet capture cannot decrypt arbitrary encrypted payloads.
Modern log alerts do not embed raw results or arbitrary custom JSON in common schema; dimensions supply context.
Invented Site Recovery vault distractor misses the important real Backup vault distinction.
Soft-delete duration is configurable from 14 to 180 days, not universally 14.
Log Analytics agent is retired; use current Azure Monitor Agent.
Main outline targets Azure-resource Site Recovery; align scenario to Azure VMs and remove an obvious AzCopy distractor.
Original mixed VMware/Azure and post-failover chronology; make protected direction explicit.
Three-only destination framing is incomplete.
Mute not universal; action groups optional.
ITSM retirement-sensitive aside unnecessary.
Azure-to-Azure uses Failover; planned/unplanned labels vary by source scenario.
SLO is not necessarily stricter than an SLA.
